sources.facts: Village newsletter issue529 identifies the flat area reached by the long approach steps as the fourth bailey, an artificially levelled enclosure. Higher ground behind the shrine is the main enclosure, outside this member.
Tourism association describes mountain castle protected by valleys, with later shrine context, rather than a standing keep.
Official elevation API describes original DEM1A,5A,5B,5C,10B no-data fallback hierarchy. Original numeric values are heights, not appearance pixels.

limits: Mapped surviving levelled fourth-bailey earthwork at Chihaya Castle: complete retained20-corner lower precinct ground surface and edge slopes, shaped by original numerical elevation values. No surviving keep is claimed. Upper enclosures, ridge ditch, modern shrine/teahouse, signs, steles, trees, whole natural hill and approach staircase are outside this constituent; whole Chihaya Castle remains unfinished. Present digital ground does not establish exact medieval construction age or original rampart/cut profile. Nominal~1m data pixels/2m review field are not accuracy guarantees.
